source_revision_stamp_note: UTC equivalent of the revision time printed in the document header ("11/14/26 05:00 PM", Eastern daylight time = UTC-4). The report does not state its own zone; ET is the zone the column header names. Retrieval time is recorded separately as fetched_at_utc - the two are never conflated, because a report retrieved hours later is still the same revision of the document.
extraction_tool: fetch_page (PDF text extraction), both chunks read in full
supersession_note: One dated snapshot of the 11/14 05:00 p.m. ET report - the first report to carry the post-deadline status for the 11/14 games and the first listing for the 11/15 games. The 11/15 06:15 a.m. ET snapshot in this directory is a later revision covering the 11/15 games; the two are diffed, never merged, and neither is labelled "latest".
extraction_notes: Game Time is printed on a 12-hour clock with no AM/PM marker (e.g. "07:00 (ET)"). The meridian for every row is read from the independent official schedule PDF's ET column for the same date and matchup; where both documents print a time for the game, the row links both.

Columns are lost at PDF page breaks. Each row records exactly which of the seven columns its own printed line carries (cells_lost), and extraction_audit counts the losses. Where Game Date or Game Time is lost but the Matchup survives, the value is repaired from the schedule PDF and both documents are cited. Where the Matchup and Team cells are lost, the row is attributed to the game and club by block position only and flagged unverified.
NOT YET SUBMITTED is a reporting state on its own row with empty player and status cells. It is never read as 'no injuries'.

The New York Knicks have no row at all for their 11/15 game at Toronto - the block prints Toronto's five rows only - and the same is true of the 11/15 06:15 a.m. report. Whether that is an exemption or a gap in the published file cannot be determined from these documents, so no New York availability status is inferred (flag P8-05).

Philadelphia's centre is printed "Embiid, Joel" here and "Embid, Joel" in the 11/15 06:15 a.m. report; Washington's forward is printed "Champagnie, Justin" here and "Champagne, Justin" there. Both spellings are stored exactly as printed and surfaced as name drift by the diff, never merged (flag P8-04).

The reason cell for the Brooklyn forward is split by the page break ("Injury/Illness - Right Calf Tightness /" at the foot of one page, "Soreness" alone at the top of the next); the two printed fragments are reassembled into one cell and flagged.
No availability probability, minute estimate, production impact or pick is stored in this file or derived from these rows.
